A study evaluating radiotherapy in myeloma found that radiation therapy contributes to pain relief, with complete relief observed in 31% of patients and partial relief in 54% of patients.
Radiation-induced fractures are rare but can occur secondary to altered skeletal physiology, and they most frequently occur in association with radiotherapy for soft tissue sarcomas.

O'Sullivan's randomized control study on patients with extremity soft tissue sarcoma revealed a 35% infection rate for patients receiving preoperative radiation versus 17% for postoperative radiation.
